blocks.text: [1] [^n2183]And when Jesus entered Jerusalem, he went up to the temple of God, and found [2] there oxen and sheep and doves. [^n2184]And when he beheld those that sold and those that bought, and the money-changers sitting, [^n2185]he made for himself a scourge of rope, and drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep and the oxen, and the money-changers; [^n2186]and he threw down their money, and upset their tables, and the seats of [3] them that sold the doves; [^n2187]and he was teaching, and saying unto them, Is it not written, My house is a house of prayer for all peoples? and ye have made it a den [4] for robbers. [^n2188]And he said unto those that sold the doves, Take this hence, and [5] make not my Father’s house a house of merchandise. [^n2189]And he suffered not any [6] one to carry vessels inside the temple. [^n2190]And his disciples remembered the scripture, [7] The zeal of thy house hath eaten me up. [^n2191]The Jews answered and said unto him, [8] What sign hast thou shewn us, that thou doest this? [^n2192]Jesus answered and said unto [9] them, Destroy this temple, and I shall raise it in three days. [^n2193]The Jews said unto him, This temple was built in forty-six years, and wilt thou raise it in three days? [10] [^n2194]But he spake unto them of the temple of his body, that when[^n2195] they destroyed it, he [11] [Arabic, p. 122] would raise it in three days. [^n2196]When therefore he rose from among the dead, his disciples remembered that he said this; and they believed the scriptures, and the word that Jesus spake.

[12] [^n2197]And when Jesus sat down over against the treasury, he observed how the multitudes were casting their offerings into the treasury: and many rich men were [13, 14] throwing in much. [^n2198]And there came a poor widow, and cast in two mites. [^n2199]And Jesus called his disciples, and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, This poor [15] widow cast into the treasury more than all the people: [^n2200]and all of these cast into the place of the offering of God[^n2201] of the superfluity of their wealth; while this woman of her want threw in all that she possessed.

[16] [^n2202]And he spake unto them this parable, concerning people who trusted in themselves [17] that they are righteous, and despised every man: [^n2203]Two men went up to the [18] temple to pray; one of them a Pharisee, and the other a publican. [^n2204]And the Pharisee stood apart,[^n2205] and prayed thus, O Lord, I thank thee, since I am not like the rest of men, the unjust, the profligate, the extortioners, or even like this publican; [19] [^n2206]but I fast two days a week, and tithe all my possessions.[^n2207] [^n2208]And the publican was [20] standing at a distance, and he would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but was [21] beating upon his breast, and saying, O Lord, have mercy on me, me the sinner. [^n2209]I say unto you, that this man went down justified to his house more than the Pharisee. Every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and every one that abaseth himself shall be exalted.

[22] [Arabic, p. 123] [^n2210]And when eventide was come, he left all the people, and went outside the [23] city to Bethany, he and his twelve, and he remained there. [^n2211]And all the people, because they knew the place, came to him, and he received them; and them that [24] had need of healing he healed. [^n2212]And on the morning of the next day, when he returned [25] to the city from Bethany, he hungered. [^n2213]And he saw a[^n2214] fig tree at a distance on the beaten highway, having on it leaves. And he came unto it, expecting to find something on it; and when he came, he found nothing on it but the leaves—it[^n2215] was not [26] the season of figs—[^n2216]and he said unto it, Henceforward for ever let no man eat fruit of thee. And his disciples heard.

[27] [^n2217]And they came to Jerusalem. And there was there a man of the Pharisees, [28] named Nicodemus, ruler of the Jews. [^n2218]This man came unto Jesus by night, and said unto him, My Master, we know that thou hast been sent from God as a teacher; and no man can do these signs that thou doest, except him whom God is [29] with. [^n2219]Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, If a man [30] be not born a second time, he cannot see the kingdom of God. [^n2220]Nicodemus said unto him, How can a man who is old be born? can he, think you, return again to [31] his mother’s womb a second time, to enter and be born? [^n2221]Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, If a man be not born of water and the Spirit, [32] he cannot enter the kingdom of God. [^n2222]For he that is born of flesh is flesh; and he that [33] is born of Spirit is spirit. [^n2223]Wonder not that I said unto thee that ye must be born a [34] [Arabic, p. 124] second time. [^n2224]The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest its voice, but thou knowest not from what place it cometh, nor whither it goeth: so [35] is every man that is born of the Spirit. [^n2225]Nicodemus answered and said unto him, [36] How can that be? [^n2226]Jesus answered and said unto him, Art thou teaching[^n2227] Israel, [37] and yet knowest not these things? [^n2228]Verily, verily, I say unto thee, What we know [38] we say, and what we have seen we witness: and ye receive not our witness. [^n2229]If I said unto you what is on earth, and ye believed not, how then, if I say unto you [39] what is in heaven, will ye believe? [^n2230]And no man hath ascended up into heaven, except him that descended from heaven, the Son of man, which is in heaven. [40] [^n2231]And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so is the Son of man to be [41] lifted up; [^n2232]so that every man who may believe in him may not perish, but have [42] eternal life. [^n2233]God so loved the world, that[^n2234] he should give his only Son; and so every one that believeth on him should not perish, but should have eternal life. [43] [^n2235]God sent not his Son into the world to judge the world; but that the world might [44] be saved by his hand. [^n2236]He that believeth in him shall not be judged: but he that believeth not is condemned beforehand, because he hath not believed in the name [45] of the only Son, the Son of God.[^n2237] [^n2238]This is the judgement, that the light came into the world, and men loved the darkness more than the light; because their deeds [46] were evil. [^n2239]Whosoever doeth evil deeds hateth the light, and cometh not to the [47] light, lest his deeds be reproved. [^n2240]But he that doeth the truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be known, that they have been done in God.

n2201.text: Lit. house of the offering of God, as in the ms. described by Gildemeister (at Luke xxi. 4); but it is simply a reproduction of the phrase used in the Peshitta at Luke xxi. 3. The parallel passages are a good deal fused together.

n2234.text: The Arabic particle means in order that. Perhaps it is a clerical error for so that; or it may be meant to represent the Syriac.

n2237.text: The translator has followed too closely the order of words in his Syriac original, which agrees with the Text. Rec.
